elements.element: No non-compete restriction on Customer (Customer not barred from developing/marketing/selling/acquiring competing products)
elements.evidence: §12.4 as revised: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

elements.element: No field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer's business
elements.evidence: §12.3 preserved: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; §12.4 restriction on "any territory" is now permissive
§12.3 untouched: "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment"

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: revised §12.4 refers to "any product or service that competes with Vendor" — no named product (no restriction remains at all)

elements.element: Restriction limited to during the term only
elements.evidence: "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" retained in the (now permissive) sentence

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions
elements.evidence: no carve-out language inserted; unnecessary because no restriction remains

reasons: The single operator swap "shall not" → "may" in §12.4 eliminates the non-compete and field/territory restriction on Customer, achieving the locked preferred level.
Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, carve-outs) are unmet but irrelevant: preferred and fallback are separate bargains and the preferred level is satisfied.
Minimality is satisfied — one operator changed, no rewrite, no new exceptions, and §12.3 untouched.

Intent preserved: the residual "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" now merely frames a permission consistent with §12.3, introducing no contradiction, undefined term, or dangling mechanic.
Margin comment correctly explains the operator change and offers the fallback without lecturing.
